RequestIdHeader.description: Correlates this response with a server log line. Echoes the caller's own 'X-Request-Id' request header when present; otherwise the server generates one. Set unconditionally on every response.

commands.description: Commands the assistant proposes. Absent when it proposes none.

AiChat.description: One chat transcript. GET /api/v1/ai/chats returns this shape without 'messages'; GET /api/v1/ai/chats/{id} returns it in full.

created.description: ISO-8601 instant the chat was created

messages.description: Messages, oldest first. Omitted from the /chats list response.

commands.description: SQL commands the assistant proposed with this reply. Present only on an assistant message that proposed at least one.

title.description: Chat title, generated from the first user message

updated.description: ISO-8601 instant of the last change

chatId.description: Existing chat to continue. A new chat is created when omitted.

database.description: Database the question is about. The caller must be authorized on it.

protocolVersion.description: Protocol version the client speaks. Rejected with 'protocol_unsupported' when unknown. Defaults to 1 when omitted.

chatId.description: Chat this exchange belongs to, for continuing the conversation

commands.description: SQL commands the assistant proposes. Absent when it proposes none.

toolCalls.description: Tools the assistant invoked while answering. Absent when it invoked none.

configured.description: True once a subscription has been activated

AiProtocolError.description: Rejected chat request. Carries the negotiation fields when the protocol version is at fault.

code.description: Machine-readable cause, 'protocol_unsupported' for a version mismatch

BatchError.description: Failed bulk load. Carries how much of the payload was attempted, because a batch is not atomic and the caller has to reconcile before retrying.

bytesRead.description: Bytes of the upload the server consumed, so a client can verify its whole file arrived - and, on a truncated load, how far the server got. Never more than the client sent.

edgesCreated.description: Edges attempted before the failure, with the same upper-bound caveat as 'verticesCreated'.

error.description: Why the load failed. Carries the offending location, such as a line number or a temporary id, because a batch failure echoes client input rather than engine internals.

exception.description: Exception class name, for distinguishing failure classes programmatically

linesRead.description: Lines the parser read, so 'linesRead' minus 'linesSkipped' can be checked against the records created

linesSkipped.description: Lines that carried no record: blank lines, plus CSV headers and '---' separators

partialCommit.description: True when earlier chunks are durably committed. Retrying the whole payload then duplicates the already-committed vertices, because temporary ids are not keys.

requestId.description: Correlation id echoing X-Request-Id, for cross-referencing the failure against the server log. Absent when the request carried no correlation id.

verticesCreated.description: Vertices attempted before the failure. An upper bound on what is durable: records handled since the last commit boundary were rolled back.

verticesWithoutId.description: Vertices created without an '@id' under refMode=id. They are loaded and durable, but no edge can reference them. Absent when zero.

bytesRead.description: Bytes of the upload the server consumed, so a client can verify its whole file arrived - and, on a truncated load, how far the server got. Never more than the client sent.

idMapping.description: Temporary id to RID mapping, present only when temporary ids were used and the mapping was small enough to echo

idMappingOmitted.description: True when the mapping was too large to return

idMappingSize.description: Number of entries in the omitted mapping

linesRead.description: Lines the parser read, so 'linesRead' minus 'linesSkipped' can be checked against the records created

linesSkipped.description: Lines that carried no record: blank lines, plus CSV headers and '---' separators

verticesWithoutId.description: Vertices created without an '@id' under refMode=id. They are loaded and durable, but no edge can reference them. Absent when zero.

BootstrapStateResponse.description: Per-database bootstrap state of one peer

error.description: Why the database could not be read. Absent on success.

fingerprint.description: Content fingerprint, empty when the database could not be read

lastTxId.description: Last transaction id, -1 when the database could not be read

ClusterActionResponse.description: Outcome of a cluster management action

database.description: Database the action applied to. Present on resync.

leaderId.description: Leader after the action. Present on leadership transfer.

localServer.description: Server that performed the action. Present on resync.

ClusterAuthSessionRequest.description: A session token and the action to apply to it

ClusterAuthSessionResponse.description: The session as held by the node that issued it

user.description: The principal the session belongs to

capabilities.description: Optional wire-format sections THIS node can decode, sorted (issue #7219)

databasePresence.description: Which peer holds which database. Present only when this server is the leader and the request set '?presence=true'.

acquireError.description: Why the last acquisition failed. Absent on success.

acquireStatus.description: State of the last acquisition attempt. Absent when none was made.

acquireTimestamp.description: When the last acquisition attempt ran, as epoch milliseconds. Absent when none was made.

bootstrapFingerprint.description: Fingerprint recorded at bootstrap. Absent when no baseline exists.

bootstrapLastTxId.description: Last transaction id recorded at bootstrap. Absent when no baseline exists.

isLeader.description: True when this server is the leader

leaderHttpAddress.description: Leader HTTP address, null when unknown

leaderReady.description: True when the leader has finished the work that makes it safe to serve writes

capabilities.description: Optional wire-format sections this peer can decode, as last observed by the leader (issue #7219). Absent on a follower, which does not poll, and on the leader for a peer it has not reached: an absent array means 'not known', which the leader treats exactly like 'cannot decode'.

httpAddress.description: Peer HTTP endpoint as resolved by this node. Absent when it cannot be resolved.

httpAddressAmbiguous.description: True when the HTTP endpoint above does not identify this peer alone: two or more peers resolve to it, which is what happens when 'http' ports are not declared in arcadedb.ha.serverList and the nodes differ by port rather than by host. Peer-to-peer operations (snapshot resync, cluster verify) refuse to dial such a peer. Absent when the address is unambiguous.

lagging.description: True when the lag exceeds the configured warning threshold. Absent for the leader's own entry and until a health sample exists.

laggingForMs.description: How long this peer has been lagging, in milliseconds. Absent for the leader's own entry and until a health sample exists.

lastContactMs.description: Milliseconds since last contact. Absent for the leader's own entry and until a health sample exists.

matchIndex.description: Highest log entry known replicated. Absent for the leader's own entry and until a health sample exists.

nextIndex.description: Next log entry to send. Absent for the leader's own entry and until a health sample exists.

replicaStatus.description: Replica health status. Absent for the leader's own entry and until a health sample exists.

replicationLag.description: Entries behind the leader. Absent for the leader's own entry and until a health sample exists.

replicationRttMs.description: Mean replication round-trip time. Absent when no sample exists.

replicationRttP99Ms.description: 99th percentile replication round-trip time. Absent when no sample exists.

version.description: Server version this peer reported alongside its capabilities. Absent when the leader has no fresh answer from it.

uptime.description: Milliseconds since the Raft server started

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to serialize into the response. When omitted, a LIMIT stated by the query is honored as written and only a query stating none is capped by the server default ('arcadedb.server.httpQueryDefaultLimit'). Use -1 for no cap. The response always reports the cap that was applied ('limit'), how many rows it carries ('returned') and whether rows were left behind ('truncated'). No value here can widen a single response past the server's hard ceiling ('arcadedb.server.httpQueryMaxResultRows'): a result that would exceed it is refused with 413 instead of being truncated.

params.description: Command parameters. Values may be JSON primitives, arrays, or typed-marker objects: {"$bytes": "<base64>"} for byte[] (standard or URL-safe base64), {"$int8": [v0, v1, ...]} for byte[] from integers in [-128, 127] (used to send INT8-encoded vectors to LSM_VECTOR indexes without a float32 round-trip).

result.description: True when the database exists and is among the authenticated user's authorized databases. False both when the database does not exist and when it exists but the caller is not authorized to see it, since the response does not distinguish the two cases.

FullTextSearchRequest.description: Full-text search over a FULL_TEXT index

indexName.description: Full-text index to search; wins over 'typeName' when both are given

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return

properties.description: Indexed properties, to pick between several full-text indexes on the same type

queryText.description: Lucene-syntax query, e.g. 'java' or '+java -python'. Must not be blank

typeName.description: Type whose full-text index to search. Usable alone only when the type carries exactly one

distance.description: Dense vector distance, lower is better. Absent on a scored hit

score.description: Sparse or full-text score, higher is better. Absent on a distance hit

similarity.description: Similarity function the index scores with, e.g. BM25

status.description: Always 'ok' when the database is reachable

from.description: Inclusive lower bound of the timestamp range. Unbounded when omitted.

maxDataPoints.description: Used with the time range to derive a bucket interval when 'aggregation.bucketInterval' is omitted.

aggregation.description: Bucketed aggregation. Omit for raw samples.

bucketInterval.description: Bucket width in the same unit as the timestamps. Derived from 'maxDataPoints' and the time range when omitted.

alias.description: Output field name. Defaults to the field name suffixed with the lower-cased aggregation type.

type.description: Aggregation function. Required, one of SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT, matched case-insensitively. A value that matches none is reported as an error frame on this target, leaving the other targets served.

fields.description: Fields to project on a raw (non-aggregated) query. All fields when omitted. Ignored when 'aggregation' is present.

refId.description: Identifier echoed back as the result key. Defaults to 'A'.

tags.description: Tag filter as name to value pairs

to.description: Inclusive upper bound of the timestamp range. Unbounded when omitted.

additionalProperties.description: Result for one target. Carries 'error' instead of frames when the target could not be resolved.

error.description: Why the target could not be resolved. Present only when it failed; 'frames' is then empty.

values.description: Column-major values, one array per field

fields.description: Fields, positionally aligned with the value arrays

name.description: Field name, 'time' for the time column

type.description: Grafana field type, for example time or number

HybridSearchRequest.description: Fused vector, full-text and graph-expansion search

expand.description: Optional graph expansion leg, seeded from the union of the retrieval legs and ranked by breadth-first discovery order.

maxDepth.description: Hops to walk from a seed

filter.description: Optional read-only SQL WHERE predicate applied to the vector leg's candidate window

fulltextIndexName.description: Full-text index the full-text leg searches. Required whenever 'fulltextQuery' is given, and refused without it

fulltextQuery.description: Lucene-syntax query for the full-text leg. Goes together with 'fulltextIndexName': half a leg is refused rather than silently dropped. Omit both to search without a full-text leg.

fusionStrategy.description: How the legs are combined. Only RRF can consume the graph expansion leg, which is ranked by traversal order

k.description: Maximum number of fused results to return

queryIndices.description: Sparse dimension ids matching the 'queryVector' weights. Requires sparse=true

queryVector.description: Query vector for the vector leg

vectorIndexName.description: Name of an LSM_VECTOR or LSM_SPARSE_VECTOR index

weights.description: Per-leg weight applied to every rank contribution. The only accepted keys are 'vector', 'fulltext' and 'expand', and a weight for a leg the request does not ask for is refused rather than ignored.

fulltextIndexName.description: Full-text index that was searched, present whenever the full-text leg ran - including when it matched nothing

fused.description: False when only one leg produced rows: fusion needs at least two sources, so the response carries that leg's native distance or score instead of a fused one.

fusionStrategy.description: Strategy actually applied; absent when 'fused' is false

legs.description: Per-leg accounting: how many rows each leg contributed, and whether the expansion hit its seed or fan-out cap

depth.description: Hops from the seed, for a hit the expansion leg contributed

distance.description: Vector distance, present instead of 'fusedScore' on an unfused dense response

fusedScore.description: Fused score, higher is better. Present when 'fused' is true

path.description: Record ids from the seed to this hit, seed included

score.description: Sparse or full-text score, present instead of 'fusedScore' on an unfused sparse or full-text response

sources.description: Which legs contributed this hit: vector, fulltext, expand

scoring.description: Scoring direction of the vector leg

sparse.description: Whether the vector leg took the sparse path

truncated.description: True when the result window was filled

token.description: Session token prefixed 'AU-', presented as a bearer token

allowedOrigins.description: Extra browser origins permitted for the HTTP transport, beyond loopback addresses which are always allowed. The value '*' permits any origin, disabling the anti-DNS-rebinding check.

allowedUsers.description: Users permitted to reach the MCP server. The value '*' permits any authenticated user.

databases.description: Per-database permission overrides, keyed by database name. Present only when at least one override is configured.

enabled.description: Whether the MCP server answers requests

principalProfiles.description: Tool profile assigned per principal (user or API token) name. Present only when at least one is configured.

McpDatabaseOverride.description: Per-database permission override. Every field is optional; an omitted field inherits the server-wide value. A permission set to true here still requires the corresponding global permission to be true, so an override can only narrow access, never widen it. 'allowedUsers' is intersected with the global 'allowedUsers', not a replacement for it.

allowAdmin.description: Restrict administrative access for this database

allowDelete.description: Restrict delete access for this database

allowInsert.description: Restrict insert access for this database

allowReads.description: Restrict read access for this database

allowSchemaChange.description: Restrict schema-change access for this database

allowUpdate.description: Restrict update access for this database

allowedUsers.description: Users permitted on this database, intersected with the global 'allowedUsers'

NdJsonBatchEvent.description: One line of a streamed bulk load. Exactly one of 'progress', 'summary' or 'error' is present.

error.description: Terminal line of a failed load: the same object the buffered encoding carries, plus the 'status' it would have been sent under. The status line cannot be taken back once the stream has started, so the status travels in band.

commitIndex.description: Last applied Raft index, present on a replicated database. On a failed load it bookmarks the chunks that were committed before the failure

status.description: HTTP status the buffered encoding would have used: 400, 408 or 500

statusMapped.description: Present and false when 'status' is the unclassified 500 fallback rather than the status the buffered encoding would have chosen - the case of an engine failure raised after the stream had already started. Key on 'exception' there, not on 'status'. Absent whenever 'status' is exact.

progress.description: A chunk acknowledgement, written while the request body is still being read. Emitted at every vertex commit and every 'commitEvery' edges. The counters are records ATTEMPTED, the same upper bound on what is durable that the partial-commit counters carry: vertices are committed at each flush, while edges are buffered and written when the load ends.

bytesRead.description: Bytes of the upload the server consumed, so a client can verify its whole file arrived - and, on a truncated load, how far the server got. Never more than the client sent.

idMapping.description: Temporary id to RID mapping of the vertices this chunk resolved, and only of those: the mapping is handed back one committed chunk at a time so neither end ever holds the whole load's worth of it (issue #7353). Concatenate the 'idMapping' of every line, in order, to obtain what the buffered encoding returns in one object, and check the total against 'idMappingSize' on the terminal line. Absent on an edge-phase acknowledgement, on a chunk whose vertices declared no @id under refMode=tempId, and when the request sent idMapping=false.

linesRead.description: Lines the parser read, so 'linesRead' minus 'linesSkipped' can be checked against the records created

linesSkipped.description: Lines that carried no record: blank lines, plus CSV headers and '---' separators

verticesWithoutId.description: Vertices created without an '@id' under refMode=id. They are loaded and durable, but no edge can reference them. Absent when zero.

summary.description: Terminal line of a successful load: the same object the buffered application/json response carries, plus 'commitIndex' on a replicated database - the read-your-writes bookmark, which cannot be a response header here because the response has already started when its value becomes known.

commitIndex.description: Last applied Raft index, the value the X-ArcadeDB-Commit-Index header carries on the buffered encoding

idMappingSize.description: Total number of temporary ids the load resolved. Check the number of mapping entries received across all the lines against it: a mapping that arrives in pieces can lose one to a truncated response without any single piece looking wrong.

idMappingStreamed.description: Always true on this encoding when the load resolved any temporary id: the mapping travelled in the 'idMapping' of the progress lines rather than in this object, so 'idMapping' here is only whatever the last chunk resolved after the final acknowledgement - usually nothing. 'idMappingOmitted' is never sent on this encoding: the size cap it reports exists because the buffered encoding has to build the whole mapping before it can send anything, which streaming removes (issue #7353).

NdJsonQueryEvent.description: One line of a newline-delimited streaming response. Exactly one of 'record', 'stats' or 'error' is present.

error.description: A failure raised after the 200 had already been sent. The status code cannot be taken back at that point, so the failure is reported in band and no 'stats' line follows.

record.description: One result row, identical to an element of the 'result' array of the buffered application/json response.

stats.description: Trailer, always the last line of a complete stream. Carries the same three numbers the buffered response reports at top level.

limit.description: Effective row cap applied while streaming, -1 when uncapped

returned.description: Number of rows that reached the client

truncated.description: True when the cap stopped the stream with rows still pending, so the result is incomplete

PeerCapabilitiesResponse.description: The wire-format sections one peer can decode

capabilities.description: Capability tokens this peer can decode, sorted

peerId.description: Peer that answered. A caller must check this against the peer it meant to ask: on a cluster that declares no explicit 'http' ports several peers can resolve to one address.

version.description: Server version of the answering peer, for operators; nothing decides on it

done.description: Units completed in the current step

operation.description: Operation name, for example CHECK DATABASE

percentage.description: Completion percentage of the current step, -1 when the total is unknown

total.description: Units in the current step, -1 when unknown

value.description: One [timestamp, value] pair: a Unix timestamp in seconds (number), then the sample value (string)

items.description: One [timestamp, value] pair: a Unix timestamp in seconds (number), then the sample value (string)

anyOf.description: One [timestamp, value] pair: a Unix timestamp in seconds (number), then the sample value (string)

result.description: Evaluation result, shaped by 'resultType': an array of instant samples when 'vector', an array of range series when 'matrix', and a single [timestamp, value] pair when 'scalar'.

resultType.description: Shape of 'result': a vector of instant samples, a matrix of range samples, or a scalar

items.description: One series as a label map, including the '__name__' label

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to serialize into the response. When omitted, a LIMIT stated by the query is honored as written and only a query stating none is capped by the server default ('arcadedb.server.httpQueryDefaultLimit'). Use -1 for no cap. The response always reports the cap that was applied ('limit'), how many rows it carries ('returned') and whether rows were left behind ('truncated'). No value here can widen a single response past the server's hard ceiling ('arcadedb.server.httpQueryMaxResultRows'): a result that would exceed it is refused with 413 instead of being truncated.

params.description: Query parameters. Values may be JSON primitives, arrays, or typed-marker objects: {"$bytes": "<base64>"} for byte[] (standard or URL-safe base64), {"$int8": [v0, v1, ...]} for byte[] from integers in [-128, 127] (used to send INT8-encoded vectors to LSM_VECTOR indexes without a float32 round-trip).

limit.description: Effective row cap applied while serializing, -1 when uncapped. This is the serializer's cap, not the query's own LIMIT: a query stating a LIMIT below the server default reports the default here, and 'returned' with 'truncated' describe what the response actually carries.

returned.description: Number of rows carried by this response. With the 'graph' serializer, whose cap counts graph elements rather than rows, it is the number of serialized vertices plus edges, and it can exceed 'limit': a single row can expand into several elements, and the expansion of the row that reaches the cap is not cut in half.

truncated.description: True when the cap stopped the serialization with rows still pending, so the response is incomplete

city.description: City reported by the proxy, when available

country.description: Country reported by the proxy, when available

issuer.description: Name of the cluster node that issued the session, when this node holds a copy of it; absent for a session this node issued

aggregations.description: Aliases of the computed aggregations, in bucket value order

TimeSeriesLatestResponse.description: Most recent sample of a series

columns.description: Column names, in sample value order

latest.description: Most recent sample, positionally aligned with 'columns'. Null when the series is empty.

aggregation.description: Bucketed aggregation. Present only when the caller wants buckets rather than raw rows.

bucketInterval.description: Bucket width in the same unit as the timestamps

items.description: One aggregation to compute over a bucket

alias.description: Output name. Defaults to the field name suffixed with the lower-cased aggregation type.

type.description: Aggregation function. Required, one of SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT, matched case-insensitively.

fields.description: Fields to project. All fields when omitted.

from.description: Inclusive lower bound of the timestamp range. Unbounded when omitted.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return for a raw (non-aggregated) query. Defaults to 20000. Ignored when 'aggregation' is present.

tags.description: Tag filter as name to value pairs. All pairs must match. A name that is no TAG column of the type is refused with 400 rather than ignored.

to.description: Inclusive upper bound of the timestamp range. Unbounded when omitted.

columns.description: Column names, in the order the row values appear

nonTimeSeriesTypes.description: Measurements naming a type that exists but is not a time-series type

requestId.description: Correlation id echoing X-Request-Id, for matching against server logs

unavailableTypes.description: Measurements naming a time-series type whose storage engine failed to load; see the server log for why

unknownTypes.description: Measurements naming a type that does not exist

TransferLeaderRequest.description: Transfer target. Send an empty object to let Raft choose. Unknown fields are rejected.

peerId.description: Peer to make leader. Raft chooses when omitted.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the transfer to complete, in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000.

VectorSearchRequest.description: kNN search over a dense or sparse vector index

efSearch.description: Dense-index search beam width: higher values improve recall at higher cost. Rejected for a sparse index

filter.description: Optional read-only SQL WHERE predicate applied to a bounded candidate set. Evaluated against each expanded neighbor row, where record properties are flattened and @rid, @type, record, plus distance (dense) or score (sparse) are available. At most4096 characters.

indexName.description: Name of an LSM_VECTOR or LSM_SPARSE_VECTOR index

k.description: Maximum number of results to return

queryIndices.description: Sparse dimension ids matching the 'queryVector' weights; omit to use the vector's own positions. Requires sparse=true

queryVector.description: Dense query vector, or the sparse weights matching 'queryIndices' when sparse is true

sparse.description: Search an LSM_SPARSE_VECTOR index instead of a dense one

VectorSearchResponse.description: Ranked neighbors of the query vector

candidateLimit.description: Size of the candidate window the search inspected, which a filter over-fetches into

distance.description: Dense vector distance, lower is better. Absent on a scored hit

score.description: Sparse or full-text score, higher is better. Absent on a distance hit

scoring.description: Which direction is better and how it was computed, e.g. 'distance_lower_is_better:COSINE' or 'score_higher_is_better:dot_product'. Read it rather than assuming, because the two paths rank in opposite directions.

sparse.description: Whether the sparse path was taken

truncated.description: True when the result window was filled, so further matches may exist. False for a short result: the search already returned every match it could find within 'candidateLimit'.

VerifyDatabaseResponse.description: Per-file checksums of one database. A follower response carries only its own 'localChecksums', 'files' and 'localServer'; the leader instead returns only 'result', nesting a cluster-wide comparison against every other peer.

files.description: Files with size and category. Present on a follower response.

localChecksums.description: File name to checksum map, for a quick cross-peer comparison. Present on a follower response.

localServer.description: Server the checksums were taken on. Present on a follower response.

result.description: Leader-only cluster-wide comparison, fanned out to every peer

files.description: The leader's files with size and category

localChecksums.description: Leader's file name to checksum map

overallStatus.description: ALL_CONSISTENT when every peer was compared and agreed, INCONSISTENCY_DETECTED when a compared peer differs, VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE when nothing diverged but at least one peer could not be verified

items.description: One peer's comparison against the leader's checksums

error.description: Why the peer could not be queried or compared. Absent on a completed comparison.

matchingFiles.description: Files whose checksum matches. Absent when the peer could not be queried.

mismatchedFiles.description: Files whose checksum differs. Absent when the peer could not be queried.

mismatches.description: Present only when mismatchedFiles is greater than zero

items.description: One file whose checksum differs between the leader and a peer

remoteChecksum.description: Peer's CRC for the file, or 'MISSING' when the peer does not have it

basicAuth.description: Basic HTTP authentication with username and password

bearerAuth.description: Token authentication. Accepts an API token prefixed 'at-', created at POST /api/v1/server/api-tokens, or a session token prefixed 'AU-', returned by POST /api/v1/login.

post.description: Exchanges a subscription key for an activation held by the server. The server sends its version and a derived hardware id to the gateway as part of the exchange, and restricts this operation to the root user because it writes server-wide configuration (config/ai.json).

requestBody.description: Subscription key

400.description: Bad request: the request body or the subscription key is missing

403.description: Forbidden: only the root user may activate

500.description: Internal server error, including a failure to reach the gateway

502.description: The gateway rejected the subscription key. Its own 401 or 403 is remapped to 502 here.

503.description: Passed through verbatim when the gateway itself answers 503

post.summary: Activate the AI assistant with a subscription key

post.description: Submits a profiler snapshot and returns the assistant's analysis plus any SQL commands it proposes. The server derives the schema of every database referenced inside 'profilerData' and forwards it to the assistant automatically; the client does not supply schemas directly.

requestBody.description: Profiler snapshot

400.description: Bad request, or the assistant is not configured

502.description: The gateway rejected the stored subscription token; remapped from the gateway's own 401 or 403

503.description: AI gateway unreachable, reported with code 'gateway_unreachable'

504.description: AI gateway timed out, reported with code 'gateway_timeout'

post.description:
Sends one message in the context of a database, optionally continuing an existing chat by 'chatId'. The server embeds the database schema and server metrics in the prompt (review-first) and always answers with a single JSON body; the reply may carry SQL commands the assistant proposes. For the client-orchestrated streaming protocol instead, use POST /api/v1/ai/chat/stream.

The assistant is a remote dependency: 503 means the gateway was unreachable and 504 that it did not answer in time. Both are retryable. A rejected subscription token answers 502, remapped from the gateway's own 401 or 403 so it cannot be mistaken for this request's own authentication failing.

requestBody.description: Chat message

200.description: Assistant reply, as a single JSON body.

400.description: Bad request: the assistant is not configured, the body or a required field is missing, or the requested protocol version is unsupported. On a version mismatch the body carries 'code' set to 'protocol_unsupported' plus the versions this server accepts; the other causes carry only 'error'.

403.description: Forbidden: the user cannot access the requested database

502.description: The gateway rejected the stored subscription token; remapped from the gateway's own 401 or 403

503.description: AI gateway unreachable, reported with code 'gateway_unreachable'

504.description: AI gateway timed out, reported with code 'gateway_timeout'

post.summary: Send a message to the AI assistant

post.description:
Sends one message in the context of a database, optionally continuing an existing chat by 'chatId', using a client-orchestrated streaming protocol so the AI gateway never has to open an inbound connection into the caller's network: the gateway emits 'tool_call' events on the response stream, the server executes each tool locally, and posts the result back to the gateway to resume the loop. The 200 response is always 'text/event-stream', never a JSON body; the closing 'done' event carries the same 'response', 'commands', and 'chatId' fields as POST /api/v1/ai/chat's JSON response. For a single non-streaming JSON reply instead, use POST /api/v1/ai/chat.

The assistant is a remote dependency: 503 means the gateway was unreachable and 504 that it did not answer in time. Both are retryable. A rejected subscription token answers 502, remapped from the gateway's own 401 or 403 so it cannot be mistaken for this request's own authentication failing.

requestBody.description: Chat message

200.description: Server-Sent Events stream of 'session', 'tool_call', 'tool_start', 'tool_end', and 'done' events.

400.description: Bad request: the assistant is not configured, the body or a required field is missing, or the requested protocol version is unsupported. On a version mismatch the body carries 'code' set to 'protocol_unsupported' plus the versions this server accepts; the other causes carry only 'error'.

403.description: Forbidden: the user cannot access the requested database

502.description: The gateway rejected the stored subscription token; remapped from the gateway's own 401 or 403

503.description: AI gateway unreachable, reported with code 'gateway_unreachable'

post.description:
Streams vertices and then edges into the database using the GraphBatch API. The body is never buffered, so a load is bounded by the server's memory only through the batching parameters below.

A batch is NOT atomic: GraphBatch commits every 'commitEvery' records, so a failure mid-stream leaves earlier chunks durably committed. A client-input failure answers 400 with 'verticesCreated', 'edgesCreated', and a 'partialCommit' flag; those counts are the records attempted before the failure and are an upper bound on what is durable. Because temporary ids are not keys, retrying the whole payload duplicates already-committed vertices.

A body that ends before its announced length answers 408 with the same partial-commit counts, never a 200 with a truncated count. Compare the returned 'bytesRead' against the bytes sent to verify a chunked upload arrived whole.

Send 'Accept: application/x-ndjson' to be acknowledged while you are still uploading. The answer is then a newline-delimited stream: a 'progress' line at every vertex commit and every 'commitEvery' edges, then exactly one 'summary' or 'error' line carrying the same object this endpoint would otherwise have returned. That is the HTTP counterpart of the per-chunk acknowledgement of the gRPC InsertBidirectional RPC. A progress line counts records attempted, the same upper bound the partial-commit counters carry. Anything else in Accept, including an absent header, returns the buffered object unchanged.

A load that fails before it has acknowledged anything still answers with its real status code and the buffered error body, because the status line has not been sent yet: the 400 and 408 below apply to a streaming request too. Only a failure raised after the first progress line is reported in band under a 200.

parameters.description: Send 'application/x-ndjson' to receive per-chunk acknowledgements while the request body is still being uploaded, instead of one object after the whole load. Anything else - including an absent header - returns the buffered application/json body unchanged.

get.description:
Reports this server's Raft role, the current leader, and per-peer replication health including match and next index, lag, and round-trip latency. Answers 503 until Raft has started, because the route is registered before the Raft server comes up.

The cluster and peer fields are server-level and readable by any authenticated user. The 'databases' array and the database-scoped 'alerts' are restricted to the databases the caller is authorized for, so a user granted one database does not learn the others.Requires RaftHAPlugin: the route is registered on every server, but answers only where high availability is configured.

parameters.description: When present with no value, 'true' or '1', includes the per-database x per-peer presence matrix in the 'databasePresence' field. Restricted to the root user, because it fans a bootstrap-state RPC out to every peer. Built only on the leader; a follower ignores it.
parameters.name: presence

post.description: Cluster-internal. A session token is held by the node that answered /api/v1/login and names that node ('AU-<server name>-<uuid>'). A peer that receives the token asks the issuer through this route whether the session is still valid ('validate', which also counts as activity on the issuer), and a logout tells every peer to drop its copy ('revoke'). Peers authenticate with the cluster token; a request that carries user credentials instead is refused with 403 (issue #7424).

requestBody.description: The token and what to do with it

200.description: The session, as the issuer holds it

404.description: The issuer does not hold this session

Restricted to the root user; peers satisfy this by forwarding as root with the cluster token.Requires RaftHAPlugin: the route is registered on every server, but answers only where high availability is configured.

Reports the optional replication wire-format sections this node can DECODE, as short stable tokens. The leader polls it on every peer of its Raft configuration and writes an optional section only when every peer has advertised it, so a rolling upgrade needs no ordering by hand (issue #7219).

A node running a release without this route answers 404, and the caller reads that as 'this peer can decode nothing optional' - which is why the route is safe to add and why no version comparison takes part in the decision.

Restricted to the root user; peers satisfy this by forwarding as root with the cluster token.Requires RaftHAPlugin: the route is registered on every server, but answers only where high availability is configured.

get.description:
Streams a consistent snapshot of one database as a ZIP archive, for a follower installing a fresh copy. The stream ends with a completeness manifest, advertised by a response header, so a consumer can tell a complete download from one truncated at an archive entry boundary. Only the root user may download a snapshot. Answers 503 when the server's concurrent-snapshot limit is already reached.

This route accepts HTTP Basic only: it is served by a handler outside the standard chain and never reads a bearer token.Requires RaftHAPlugin: the route is registered on every server, but answers only where high availability is configured.

200.description: ZIP archive of the database, ending with a completeness manifest

403.description: Forbidden: only the root user may download a snapshot

get.description:
Returns the per-file checksums of the database as a snapshot download would produce it, read through the same point-in-time window. Only the root user may read them.

This is an operator diagnostic: it answers "do these two nodes hold the same bytes?" without transferring a database. Resync itself does not consult it - a follower that falls behind the compacted Raft log always downloads the full snapshot ZIP - because a whole-file comparison is the wrong granularity for an ArcadeDB database, which is usually dominated by one bucket file that any single changed byte re-ships in full. Incremental resync is tracked as a page-level diff in #6115.

This route accepts HTTP Basic only, for the same reason as the snapshot download.Requires RaftHAPlugin: the route is registered on every server, but answers only where high availability is configured.
get.summary: Read the checksums of a snapshot's files

This operation takes no request body: the credentials travel on the header, and geolocation metadata is read from the CF-IPCountry, CF-IPCity, CF-Connecting-IP, X-Forwarded-For, and User-Agent headers when a proxy supplies them (each is stored truncated to 256 characters). Accepts one JSON-RPC 2.0 request, notification, or response, or a batch of them as a top-level array, and answers with the corresponding response. The method set and the parameter and result shapes for each method are defined by the Model Context Protocol specification, not by this API, so request and response bodies are not enumerated here.

The route is always registered; when the MCP server is disabled the request is refused at request time with 503, which is what makes runtime toggling possible without a restart. A request carrying only notifications and/or responses receives 202 with no body, because JSON-RPC forbids replying to those. Every other outcome, including a JSON-RPC-level error such as an unknown method or a malformed request body, is reported inside a 200 response: JSON-RPC layers its own error reporting over the HTTP transport, so a non-200 status is reserved for transport-level failures such as missing credentials, a disallowed browser Origin, an unauthorized user, an unsupported HTTP method, or the server being disabled. Requires MCPPlugin: present in every standard distribution, absent from a custom build that excludes the MCP module.

requestBody.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 request, notification, or response, or a batch of them as a top-level array

200.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 response, carrying either a 'result' or an 'error' member per the JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope. A batch request answers with an array of these.

202.description: Accepted, no body. The request carried only notifications and/or JSON-RPC responses, which this server never answers.

401.description: Unauthorized: no credentials were supplied. Raised by the HTTP layer before the request reaches the MCP dispatcher, so the body is this API's standard error shape.

403.description: Forbidden, reported as a JSON-RPC error envelope: either the request's Origin header failed the anti-DNS-rebinding check, or the authenticated user is not on the MCP server's allowedUsers list.

405.description: Method not allowed, reported as a JSON-RPC error envelope. This endpoint accepts POST only.

503.description: The MCP server is currently disabled, reported as a JSON-RPC error envelope.

post.summary: Exchange a JSON-RPC message with the MCP server

post.description:
Applies a partial configuration update: send only the fields to change. The update is all-or-nothing: every field is parsed and validated before the first one is assigned, so a payload rejected on any field leaves the configuration exactly as it was. Restricted to the root user.

Answers with the full configuration as it stands after the update. Requires MCPPlugin: present in every standard distribution, absent from a custom build that excludes the MCP module.

requestBody.description: Partial configuration. Omitted fields keep their current value.

parameters.name: time

parameters.description: How far back to look for a sample, as a duration such as '5m'. Defaults to the server setting.
parameters.name: lookback_delta

400.description: Bad request, in the Prometheus error envelope

get.summary: Evaluate a PromQL expression at a single instant

get.description: Evaluates a PromQL expression at every step across a range. Compatible with the Prometheus /api/v1/query_range endpoint. 'step' must be positive; a non-positive step answers 400.

parameters.description: Inclusive range start as a Unix timestamp in seconds, fractional seconds allowed
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: Inclusive range end as a Unix timestamp in seconds, fractional seconds allowed
parameters.name: end

parameters.description: Evaluation interval, either a plain number of seconds or a duration such as '1m'
parameters.name: step

parameters.description: How far back to look for a sample, as a duration such as '5m'. Defaults to the server setting.
parameters.name: lookback_delta

400.description: Bad request, in the Prometheus error envelope

get.summary: Evaluate a PromQL expression over a time range

get.description: Returns the label sets of the series matching the given selectors. Compatible with the Prometheus /api/v1/series endpoint. Each returned object is a label map including the '__name__' label. A selector that fails to parse is skipped rather than rejected, so a mix of valid and malformed 'match[]' values still returns the matches from the valid ones.

parameters.description: Series selector. Repeatable: every occurrence is evaluated and the results are unioned.
parameters.name: match[]

parameters.description: Inclusive range start as a Unix timestamp in seconds, fractional seconds allowed
parameters.name: start

parameters.description: Inclusive range end as a Unix timestamp in seconds, fractional seconds allowed
parameters.name: end

400.description: Bad request, in the Prometheus error envelope

post.description: Accepts a Prometheus remote-read request: a protobuf ReadRequest message compressed with Snappy block format. Answers with a Snappy-compressed protobuf ReadResponse. Configure this endpoint as a remote_read target in prometheus.yml.

requestBody.description: Snappy-compressed protobuf ReadRequest, per the Prometheus remote-read specification

400.description: Bad request: database parameter missing, body empty, or not Snappy-compressed

post.summary: Read samples through Prometheus remote read

post.description: Accepts a Prometheus remote-write request: a protobuf WriteRequest message compressed with Snappy block format. Configure this endpoint as a remote_write target in prometheus.yml. A time series is auto-created from the metric name and labels on first write. Answers 204 with no body once the samples are applied; an empty write request also answers 204.

requestBody.description: Snappy-compressed protobuf WriteRequest, per the Prometheus remote-write specification

400.description: Bad request: database parameter missing, body empty, or not Snappy-compressed

post.summary: Ingest samples through Prometheus remote write

post.description:
Reads samples from a time-series type over a timestamp range, optionally filtered by tag and projected to a subset of fields.

The response shape depends on the request: without 'aggregation' it carries raw rows under 'rows'; with 'aggregation' it carries fixed-interval buckets under 'buckets' and names the computed aggregations under 'aggregations'.

requestBody.description: Query definition

200.description: Samples, raw or aggregated according to the request

400.description: Bad request. A name in 'tags' that is no TAG column of the type is refused here, naming it and listing the type's declared TAG columns: dropping it would widen the query to the whole range, which is indistinguishable from a filter that matched everything.

413.description: The rows or buckets exceed 'arcadedb.server.httpQueryMaxResultRows': narrow the range, widen 'bucketInterval', or page the query

post.summary: Query samples, optionally aggregated into buckets

post.description:
Ingests one or more samples expressed in InfluxDB Line Protocol. The measurement name selects the time-series type, tags select the series, and fields carry the values.

The body may be gzip-compressed by sending Content-Encoding: gzip. A fully accepted request answers 204 with no body; a request whose samples could not all be applied answers 400 with the counts of what was written and dropped, so a client can tell a total rejection from a partial one.

parameters.description: Unit of the timestamps in the body. Defaults to nanoseconds when omitted.
parameters.name: precision

requestBody.description: InfluxDB Line Protocol text, one measurement per line. Optionally gzip-compressed.

400.description: Samples rejected, with the counts written and dropped

post.summary: Ingest samples in InfluxDB Line Protocol

post.description:
Runs a Lucene-syntax query against an ArcadeDB FULL_TEXT index and returns the matching documents ranked by score, highest first.

Address the index either by 'indexName', or by 'typeName' with optional 'properties'; 'indexName' wins when both are supplied. Because the limit is pushed down per bucket, a hit deleted between the index scan and the record load is skipped rather than back-filled, so a search can legitimately return fewer than 'limit' results.

requestBody.description: Full-text search request

post.summary: Full-text search over a FULL_TEXT index

post.description:
Fuses a vector retrieval leg, an optional full-text retrieval leg and an optional depth-limited graph expansion leg into one ranked list, using the engine's own vector.fuse rather than a re-implementation.

Fusion needs at least two sources. A request naming only the vector leg reports 'fused': false and returns that leg's native distance or score rather than a fabricated fused one. The expansion leg is ranked by traversal order and carries no score, so it can only be fused with the RRF strategy.

requestBody.description: Hybrid search request

200.description: Fused results, best first, each naming the legs it came from

post.summary: Fused vector, full-text and graph-expansion search

post.description:
Returns the nearest neighbors of a pre-computed query vector in a dense LSM_VECTOR or sparse LSM_SPARSE_VECTOR index. ArcadeDB does not generate embeddings: the caller supplies the vector.

Dense results expose a 'distance' (lower is better); sparse results expose a 'score' (higher is better), and 'scoring' names which of the two the response carries. A filtered search inspects a bounded candidate window whose size is reported as 'candidateLimit', so 'truncated' means the window was filled and more matches may exist - raise 'k' to see them.

requestBody.description: Vector search request

post.summary: kNN search over a vector index

get.description:
Exposes the server's metrics in the Prometheus text exposition format, for a Prometheus scrape_config to poll.

Authentication can be turned off for this route with arcadedb.serverMetrics.prometheus.requireAuthentication=false, which is how most scrape setups run it.Requires PrometheusMetricsPlugin: absent unless the metrics plugin is enabled.

200.description: Metrics in the Prometheus text exposition format

401.description: Unauthorized: returned only when the plugin requires authentication

403.description: Forbidden: unsupported or malformed Authorization header
